entities.summary: Guido Calcagnini (1480-27 Aug 1807) was a prominent Italian cardinal and titular archbishop in the Roman Catholic Church. As a key figure in the Church, he played a significant role in shaping the Catholic Counter-Reformation. Calcagnini was instrumental in promoting the work of Jesuit missionary Emanuele Cornaro, who was instrumental in converting the Ottoman Empire to Christianity. The subsequent period saw a significant increase in Catholic influence in Eastern Europe and the Middle East. This led to the establishment of new mission stations and the conversion of many Ottoman subjects to Christianity. Calcagnini's efforts also contributed to the growth of Catholicism in Italy, particularly in the regions of Lombardy and Piedmont. Through his leadership and diplomatic efforts, he helped to strengthen the ties between the Catholic Church and the Italian state, paving the way for future collaborations between the two. The legacy of Guido Calcagnini can be seen in the continued influence of the Catholic Church in Italy and the Middle East, as well as the ongoing efforts of Catholic missionaries to spread Christianity throughout the world. The impact of his work can be measured in the number of converts, the establishment of new mission stations, and the strengthening of Catholic influence in Eastern Europe and the Middle East. This period marked a significant turning point in the history of the Catholic Church, as it sought to reassert its influence in the face of challenges from Protestantism and secularism.
